tools.name: ask_business
tools.description:
Ask the store a question about its policies and services: returns, refunds and exchanges, shipping and delivery, privacy, terms, subscriptions, contact details and opening hours, or FAQ topics such as gift wrapping. The store answers it: from its own knowledge base when the store offers Ask, otherwise from its published policies, FAQ pages and articles. Put the shopper's question in ask.query in their own words, one question per call; name the topic when the shopper only implies it (e.g. a question about sending back a gift is a returns question). Read-only: it does not change the cart, place orders, or start returns. For products, prices and availability, use search_catalog or get_product.
Examples of questions:
  - What is your return policy?
  - How long does shipping to Canada take?
  - What is your phone number?
  - What are your hours of operation?
  - Do you offer gift wrapping?

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use create_cart or update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Create the shopper's cart with the given items, for a shopper whose cart has no items yet. It is the tool for a shopper asking to add or buy something when the cart is empty, and that request is all the authorization it needs. Each line item names a ProductVariant GID in item.id (variant_id from search_catalog or browse_store, or variants[].id from get_product for specific options) and a quantity; every item from one request fits in one call. When the cart already has items, nothing is created or changed: the result is that existing cart with an error message, and update_cart can extend it with its current lines plus the new ones. Returns the whole resulting cart, including its id and line ids. Repeating a call with the same items leaves the cart as it is.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the shopper's current cart: its id, every line (line id, product and variant titles, variant id, handle, URL, image, unit price, quantity, line price) and the totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. It is also where a change to an existing cart starts from: update_cart takes the cart's id and the complete set of lines the cart should hold, and create_cart applies only to a cart with no items. Works from any page.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare a cart change — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use create_cart or update_cart for that. To view a specific variant (color/size/etc.) in the browser, use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. To add a specific variant to the cart, call get_product with catalog.selected_options to get its variant id. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

tools.name: get_ucp_profile
tools.description: Get this store's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) profile, as served at /.well-known/ucp: the UCP version, the services the store offers with their endpoints (e.g. the store's UCP MCP server), its capabilities, and its payment handlers. Use it to discover how to continue a purchase with this store over UCP, or to check which platform operates the store. Read-only; works from any page.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use create_cart or update_cart for cart changes. Each product carries variant_id, its selected or first available variant. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to get that variant's id, or use show_variant to display it.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use create_cart or update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result confirms the destination, and no further navigation is needed to show it.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description:
Set the shopper's cart to exactly the given line items. This is a full replacement, not a patch: afterwards the cart holds these lines and only these.
- A listed line with its line_items[].id keeps its place and is set to the given quantity, which is absolute (2 means 2, not 2 more).
- A listed item without a line id is added, or, when that variant is already on one line of the cart, sets that line's quantity.
- A line in the cart that is not listed is removed.
It takes the cart's lines as most recently returned by get_cart, create_cart or update_cart. When the cart has changed since then (for example, the shopper edited it on the page, or a new cart replaced it), or an id is given that is not the shopper's current cart, nothing changes and the result is the current cart with an error message. Since the outcome depends only on the lines sent, repeating a call leaves the cart as it is. An empty line_items list empties the cart; leaving line_items out leaves the lines as they are. Returns the whole resulting cart, including its line ids, and messages about the call.
